memo.verdict: Neutral; park. SBM Offshore (SBMO-NL), Triaging record v1, 2026-10-07. The case is a business-model transition in a first-rank offshore contractor caught after its first leg has paid: at EUR 34.94 the shares already pay for the delivered change, and the modal return is 14.6 percent a year over eighteen months and 11.0 percent a year over three years with the multiple held at 8.5x, short of the 20 percent bar. Two re-entry triggers: a price below about EUR 28 (the three-year path clears 20 percent a year at a held multiple), or two awards inside twelve months with the multiple still near 8.5x (the modal path moves toward ING's earnings and clears the bar). Conviction: medium on the business, medium on the arithmetic, a working hypothesis on the award rate. The gate line does not park the case (management B, business quality B, predictability C, trackability C); the return does. Not invalidated: the counter-case sets the floor on the multiple and the ceiling on the rating, not a bearish view.
case: - The change is internal, broad and real, and it has travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain. An insider succession (April 2024) led to the Sale & Operate and Build-Operate-Transfer shift, thirteen speculative hulls, portfolio pruning (Aseng, Thunder Hawk, Kikeh, One Guyana, 45 percent of Chalchi), two 2026 guidance raises and a USD 2.1bn distribution floor; it shows in the key operating metrics, the statements and the estimates. Nothing remains to propagate, so the thesis must rest on new awards, which are client decisions, not internal forces.

- The external forces net to neutral: deepwater capital spending rising about 12 percent a year to 2029 with breakevens of USD 20 to 35 a barrel (tailwind, B), against shipyard scarcity (orderbooks 4.3 years; D) and Asian-yard and MODEC competition bidding full scopes and on price (D); client preference for Sale & Operate is the enabling force (B) and also lets ExxonMobil buy out the annuity early.

- The outputs the market now values are a one-off peak. FY2026 earnings per share of about USD 6.1 carry the USD 608m One Guyana gain; FY2027 falls to about USD 4.6 (consensus USD 4.47); FY2028 about USD 5.1. The engine grows beneath (about USD 2.8 ex-gain in FY2026 to USD 4.6), but the headline the band tests falls for eighteen months and compounds at about 9.8 percent a year over three years from FY2025.
counter_case: SBM is a false friend. The windfalls are real but one-off: USD 608m on One Guyana and Sale & Operate milestones pulled forward, and they come from selling the annuity that made the company defensive. Three Guyana units (Liza Unity, Prosperity, One Guyana) have already been bought out; the Lease & Operate EBITDA margin is already 46 percent from 50 percent; ING models lease gross margins at 45 to 46 percent by 2030-31; consensus Lease and Operate EBITDA is flat at about USD 930m to 990m through three years. What replaces the annuity is lump-sum construction at 15 to 20 percent margins, won on price (SEAP at USD 3.7bn against MODEC's USD 5.3bn; tendering heavily price-driven; Petrobras tenders start every bid at zero), executed in congested Chinese yards (orderbooks 4.3 years, the longest since March 2009; CMHI Jiangsu at nine times its historical maximum output; docks booked through 2029; a fatal subcontractor incident in June 2026), with five builds at once and the six-project benchmark just abandoned, while Asian yards (Hanwha Ocean on Venus; Seatrium on P-84 and P-85; CIMC Raffles's first EPCIC) move downstream into SBM's scope and MODEC recovers. The company's own history holds a 35 percent overrun (Frade, 2008) and a USD 470m termination (Yme, 2013) from the last time it bid aggressively into an upcycle; the research's highest-plausibility failure mode is yard congestion delaying milestone recognition, and a USD 450m working-capital build the sell-side had not modelled has already appeared. The earnings cannot be read: IFRS net profit exceeded Directional by USD 253m in FY2025; finance-lease treatment lifted IFRS equity by USD 1,885m; four FY2025 earnings-per-share bases run from USD 3.31 to USD 5.92 against Directional USD 3.85; no turnkey profit is recognised below 25 percent progress; the dashboard tracks the FY2027 trough year, and the FY2027 fall of about 25 percent will read as deterioration. The company has never been paid a market multiple for its quality in a decade in which its operating record was among the best in the sector (implied cost of equity 24 percent), and the thesis asks that to change now that its earnings are lumpier and its annuity shorter; the five-year range is 4.95x to 13.63x and the last re-rating, from the 10th percentile to the 66th in a year, consumed the delivered news. The backlog has historically struggled to generate attractive returns; return on invested capital is 15 percent, not 25 to 30; cash conversion was negative in each of FY2019-23 on FactSet's definition. Individually tolerable weaknesses stack on one fault line: two clients at 88 percent of revenue, two basins at 93 percent of EBITDA, three Chinese yards for every hull, a cost base in four currencies against dollar revenue, a 24 percent HAL block, a bribery history closed only in 2018, and the top team entirely internal with no external executive record. The bear multiple is the European peers' 3x to 5x EV/EBITDA, giving Morgan Stanley's EUR 15.30, 57 percent downside; no division covers the enterprise value on any multiple in the files (Lease and Operate EBITDA of USD 988m at 3x to 5x gives USD 2.96bn to USD 4.94bn against a Directional enterprise value of about USD 10.5bn and FactSet's lease-inclusive USD 14,758m). On the drop-through sensitivity the return is an F on both horizons; at the five-year 25th percentile multiple it is negative. The opposite counter, that the record is over-cautious and a company with a USD 35.6bn backlog, 1.6x leverage, a 7 percent distribution yield, the best operating record in its segment and a 20 percent-plus free-cash-flow yield at 8.4x earnings is a B case whatever the FY2027 optics, is also carried: the record concedes the operating record and the yield and answers that the free-cash-flow yield counts cash that first amortises USD 3.3bn of project debt and the proceeds of selling the annuity, and that the multiple can be 6x as easily as 10x.

Our response, as the record gives it: concede the one-off peak, the annuity erosion, the mix-driven margin decline, the earnings-basis opacity, the yard concentration and the price-led SEAP win; these are why the 'Investment Thesis' is a C, the 'Modal return' a D and the mark-to-market risk a D. Do not concede decay: the backlog is USD 35.6bn contracted to 2050 with USD 8.0bn of net cash and more than 95 percent of the lease book fixed-price; breakevens of USD 20 to 35 a barrel keep the clients producing and paying through a downturn; uptime of 98.9 percent is why those clients re-hire; the client that buys early keeps SBM as operator and keeps ordering (Longtail); the deleveraging to 1.6x is cash in the bank. The counter-case sets the floor on the multiple and the ceiling on the rating; it does not describe a business in decay.
triggers: - Re-entry trigger 1: price below about EUR 28 (the three-year path clears 20 percent a year at a held 8.5x); between EUR 28 and EUR 33 only the eighteen-month test clears.

- Re-entry trigger 2: two awards inside twelve months with the multiple still near 8.5x; the modal path then moves toward ING's earnings and clears the bar. Longtail conversion (probable, 70 percent) expected within six months; a second award by end-2027 plausible (50 percent). Alarm: no award in twelve months.
- Invalidate: two consecutive sweet-spot tenders lost on price (win rate on the next three; losing two of three resets 2027-28). Risk alarm: one of the next three lost on price.

- Turnkey EBITDA margin: our modal case 15 to 18 percent through 2027-28 (consensus two-year-forward segment margin about 13 percent; H1 2026 21.9 percent flattered). Alarm below 15 percent in one half; Invalidate below 15 percent for two consecutive halves.

- The multiple: held at about 8.5x; re-rating to 9.7x possible (35 percent), needing two awards and the FY2027 base read as the trough; a multiple holding above 9x through a flat-earnings FY2027 print would change our mind. Alarm: below the five-year 25th percentile of 6.39x with earnings unchanged.
- Yard execution: Invalidate at Directional net leverage above 2.0x from slow milestone cash or unallocated hulls; alarm on leverage rising from 1.6x.
